- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive or volatile; reduce initial forecast peaks if sentiment is weak or negative.
- Underestimate downward trends after spikes; model should anticipate mean reversion with sentiment decay, especially when sentiment drops below 0.2.
- Avoid over-optimism in 30-day forecasts when recent sentiment is low (e.g., <0.18) — adjust downward by 2–5% relative to prior forecast.
- If sentiment is consistently low or negative, reduce forecast volatility and shift toward historical mean or 10-day moving average.
- When sentiment is high but price declines sharply, model should not overcorrect — allow for lagged correction (e.g., 2–3 days delay in price drop recognition).
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 5–7 days show strong upward movement, reduce forecast by 3–8% in the 8th–10th day to account for momentum decay.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model should not overpredict 30-day peak — cap forecast at 1.5x recent 10-day high unless sentiment >0.45.
- When sentiment is low and price is falling, model should not underestimate the depth of the drop — add 1–2% buffer below true low to avoid underprediction.
